name: Scaled dot-product attention
problem: How can each token mix information from relevant tokens without recurrence?
idea: Project Q, K, V; apply scaled similarity, a causal mask when decoding, then softmax-weighted value mixing.
buy: Exact, expressive token-to-token retrieval; highly parallel training.
give: Quadratic N×N interactions; long decoding grows KV memory linearly with N.
choose: Small/medium contexts; accuracy-first reference; base for other designs.
sourceTitle: Attention Is All You Need

name: Sinusoidal positions
problem: Self-attention alone cannot tell which token came first.
idea: Add deterministic sine/cosine features at different frequencies to token embeddings.
buy: No learned position table; compact and deterministic.
give: Long-range extrapolation remains unreliable; periodic phase ambiguity.
choose: Simple baselines and architectures not using rotary position.
sourceTitle: Attention Is All You Need
note: First Transformer paper proposed sinusoids and compared learned positional embeddings.

name: Learned absolute positions
problem: A fixed position formula may be less adaptive to training data.
idea: Learn a vector per position and add it to the token embedding; considered alongside sinusoids in the 2017 Transformer paper.
buy: Flexible position representation within trained positions.
give: Fixed table typically cannot directly cover unseen positions; weak extrapolation.
choose: Known maximum context and straightforward finetuning.
sourceTitle: Attention Is All You Need (learned variant)
note: The 2017 paper discusses learned embeddings as an alternative; this is not a claim that Transformers invented all learned position embeddings.

name: Local neighborhood attention
problem: Dense self-attention is prohibitively costly on large images.
idea: Restrict a query to a spatially local neighborhood; an early concrete local self-attention design.
buy: Less computation; preserves local texture.
give: Long-range dependencies need layers, dilation, or other global routes.
choose: Vision and strongly local sequence tasks.
sourceTitle: Image Transformer
note: Earlier local-neighborhood attention milestone; distinct from Longformer’s text sliding window.

name: Relative position representations
problem: Absolute positions do not directly encode token-to-token distance.
idea: Add relative-distance representations to key/value interactions.
buy: Shift-aware distance modeling; better relative ordering.
give: Can incur distance-bias and implementation overhead; clipping loses exact far distances.
choose: Tasks needing stable local and relative relations.
sourceTitle: Self-Attention with Relative Position Representations

name: Sparse Transformer
problem: Full N² attention blocks longer sequences.
idea: Use structured sparse factorization (local and strided patterns).
buy: Reduces dense quadratic load; longer inputs.
give: Fixed sparse layouts may miss salient pairs; specialized patterns.
choose: Long structured sequences with predictable dependencies.
sourceTitle: Generating Long Sequences with Sparse Transformers

name: Multi-query attention (MQA)
problem: Autoregressive decoding repeatedly loads large K/V caches for every head.
idea: Keep many query heads but share a single K head and single V head.
buy: Major KV-cache and memory-bandwidth savings.
give: Sharing one KV head can reduce output quality versus full MHA.
choose: High-concurrency low-latency model serving.
sourceTitle: Fast Transformer Decoding: One Write-Head is All You Need

name: Compressive Transformer
problem: Attention over a fixed-size memory forgets older events entirely.
idea: Move aged memories to an additional compressed bank for longer-term access.
buy: Extends accessible history under bounded storage.
give: Compression loses detail; training and reconstruction objectives add complexity.
choose: Long temporal streams when approximate older memory is acceptable.
sourceTitle: Compressive Transformers for Long-Range Sequence Modelling

name: Explicit top-k sparse attention
problem: Softmax often spends probability mass on irrelevant connections.
idea: Keep the highest attention logits for each query; mask the rest before softmax.
buy: Concentrates attention on strongest candidates.
give: Naive full top-k ranking still computes N² scores; selection can discard relevant weak signals.
choose: Selective sparse attention when an efficient candidate-selection path is available.
sourceTitle: Explicit Sparse Transformer: Concentrated Attention Through Explicit Selection
note: Different from top-k token sampling used during final decoding.

name: Sliding-window + global attention
problem: Most neighboring tokens matter, but long documents cannot fit dense attention.
idea: Longformer combines fixed local windows with selected global tokens.
buy: Near-linear locality with global anchors for important tokens.
give: Distant non-global tokens cannot directly interact in one layer.
choose: Document understanding and locally structured long text.
sourceTitle: Longformer: The Long-Document Transformer

name: Linear attention
problem: Dense softmax needs quadratic interactions or growing KV history.
idea: Rewrite compatible attention kernels using feature maps and associativity; maintain a recurrent state.
buy: Linear sequence scaling and fixed-sized recurrent state.
give: Not identical to softmax; retrieval/associative recall can suffer.
choose: Very long streaming sequences when throughput is primary.
sourceTitle: Transformers are RNNs: Fast Autoregressive Transformers with Linear Attention

name: BigBird
problem: Pure local attention cannot express some distant dependencies.
idea: Mix local, random, and global links in a sparse attention graph.
buy: Long-document reachability; strong theoretical expressivity.
give: Complex sparse kernels and randomness; not dense exact attention.
choose: Long documents with both local and global cues.
sourceTitle: Big Bird: Transformers for Longer Sequences

name: Performer (FAVOR+)
problem: Can linear attention approximate softmax more faithfully?
idea: Use positive orthogonal random features to estimate softmax kernels.
buy: Linear space/time with theoretical approximation guarantees.
give: Finite-feature approximation errors; increased variance or numerical sensitivity.
choose: Long sequences where near-softmax behavior at lower memory matters.
sourceTitle: Rethinking Attention with Performers

name: Rotary position embeddings (RoPE)
problem: Absolute learned position tables and plain sinusoids do not elegantly encode relative displacement in Q/K.
idea: Rotate paired Q/K channels by a position-dependent angle so dot products reflect relative offsets.
buy: Relative-offset structure, no position lookup table; widely adopted.
give: Rotations alias and extrapolation deteriorates outside trained context.
choose: Default dense LLMs where positional structure matters.
sourceTitle: RoFormer: Enhanced Transformer with Rotary Position Embedding

name: ALiBi
problem: Position embedding schemes extrapolate poorly to unseen lengths.
idea: Add distance-dependent, head-specific linear biases directly to attention logits.
buy: Simple extrapolation and no position vector cache.
give: Bias prescribes recency prior; can underweight distant clues.
choose: Length generalization with a strong recency bias.
sourceTitle: Train Short, Test Long: Attention with Linear Biases Enables Input Length Extrapolation

name: FlashAttention
problem: Even exact attention wastes time moving N×N intermediates through GPU memory.
idea: Tile and fuse online-softmax attention to reduce expensive high-bandwidth-memory traffic.
buy: Exact attention semantics, much lower activation memory and faster kernels.
give: Still quadratic arithmetic; hardware and kernel constraints matter.
choose: Almost any dense attention model on supported hardware.
sourceTitle: FlashAttention: Fast and Memory-Efficient Exact Attention with IO-Awareness
formula: exact softmax with tiled IO-aware kernel
note: FlashAttention does not convert dense N² arithmetic into linear compute.

name: Grouped-query attention (GQA)
problem: MQA caches little but its single KV head can lose quality.
idea: Share K/V only within groups of query heads; intermediate KV-head count.
buy: Quality/cache balance between MHA and MQA.
give: Still less KV diversity than MHA; group sizes are model choices.
choose: Practical general-purpose LLM serving.
sourceTitle: GQA: Training Generalized Multi-Query Transformer Models from Multi-Head Checkpoints
note: Queries remain distinct per query head; K and V are shared inside each group.

name: Position Interpolation (PI)
problem: RoPE frequencies fail on position indices far outside the training window.
idea: Rescale position indices into the original trained range.
buy: Low-cost context extension with brief finetuning.
give: Compresses short-distance resolution; new context does not guarantee usable retrieval.
choose: Retrofit pretrained RoPE models to longer context.
sourceTitle: Extending Context Window of Large Language Models via Positional Interpolation

name: NTK-aware RoPE scaling
problem: Uniform position interpolation erases high-frequency local position detail.
idea: Change RoPE base across frequency bands to spread interpolation unevenly.
buy: Practical inference-time length extension with better local detail.
give: Community technique; no guarantee of faithful very-long-context retrieval.
choose: Experimentally extend existing RoPE checkpoints with validation.
sourceTitle: NTK-Aware Scaled RoPE — original bloc97 post
note: Link opens the original bloc97 post. Its June 29, 2023 timing was cross-checked with a contemporary ExLLaMA GitHub issue; no invented arXiv paper.

name: RetNet retention
problem: Need parallel training but bounded, fast recurrent inference.
idea: Retention admits parallel, recurrent, and chunkwise implementations.
buy: Constant-state decoding; hardware-friendly chunking.
give: Not softmax attention; retrieval depends on retained state.
choose: Low-latency long-run sequence modeling.
sourceTitle: Retentive Network: A Successor to Transformer for Large Language Models

name: FlashAttention-2
problem: The first FlashAttention still underuses high-end GPU execution units.
idea: Improve thread-block partitioning, parallelization and non-matmul instructions.
buy: Better utilization while retaining exact attention.
give: Device-dependent kernels; no reduction in dense theoretical FLOPs.
choose: High-throughput training and inference on supported GPUs.
sourceTitle: FlashAttention-2: Faster Attention with Better Parallelism and Work Partitioning

name: YaRN
problem: Long-window RoPE fine-tuning is costly and naive scaling damages frequency structure.
idea: Combine frequency-dependent interpolation with attention scaling and efficient adaptation.
buy: Extends pretrained contexts with relatively few training tokens.
give: Requires calibration/finetuning; longer context still needs memory and testing.
choose: Context upgrades on trained RoPE models.
sourceTitle: YaRN: Efficient Context Window Extension of Large Language Models

name: PagedAttention (vLLM)
problem: Large KV caches waste memory through fragmentation and duplicate copies during serving.
idea: Manage KV blocks using virtual-memory-style paging and block tables.
buy: Higher batch capacity and cache reuse without altering attention math.
give: Block-management overhead and serving-system complexity.
choose: Multi-user LLM inference; high-throughput serving.
sourceTitle: Efficient Memory Management for Large Language Model Serving with PagedAttention
formula: logical KV blocks → physical cache pages

name: Attention sinks / StreamingLLM
problem: Plain sliding-window eviction makes models unstable when initial attention-heavy tokens vanish.
idea: Preserve a few initial sink-token KV states plus the recent KV window.
buy: Stable bounded-cache streaming beyond the trained window.
give: Old non-sink facts are forgotten; stable generation ≠ full million-token recall.
choose: Endless conversations and streaming with limited memory.
sourceTitle: Efficient Streaming Language Models with Attention Sinks
formula: KV = first S tokens + last W tokens

name: Ring Attention
problem: A single GPU cannot store extremely long exact-attention sequences.
idea: Shard sequence blocks over multiple devices, rotating KV blocks and overlapping communication.
buy: Much longer exact attention distributed across devices.
give: Requires multiple accelerators and fast interconnect; still dense math.
choose: Distributed long-context training and evaluation.
sourceTitle: Ring Attention with Blockwise Transformers for Near-Infinite Context

name: DeepSeek Multi-head Latent Attention (MLA)
problem: Even GQA KV caches are expensive at high head counts and long context.
idea: Compress token KV information into a learned low-rank latent with a separate positional component.
buy: Much smaller stored cache with reconstruction-compatible attention.
give: Architectural/training complexity; quality depends on latent bottleneck.
choose: Large production models when KV bandwidth dominates.
sourceTitle: DeepSeek-V2: A Strong, Economical, and Efficient Mixture-of-Experts Language Model
formula: KV cache ≈ latent c_KV + RoPE component

name: DeltaNet / delta rule
problem: Additive recurrent linear attention overwrites associations imprecisely.
idea: Correct fast-weight memory with error-based delta updates instead of only accumulating values.
buy: More precise associative updates than simple linear attention.
give: Constant state is capacity-limited; implementation/training complexity.
choose: Streaming systems where state is small but write quality matters.
sourceTitle: Parallelizing Linear Transformers with the Delta Rule over Sequence Length
note: The delta learning rule predates 2024; this date is for the scalable DeltaNet transformer implementation.

name: Differential Transformer
problem: Softmax attends to distracting context even when stronger signals exist.
idea: Subtract one learned attention distribution from another to cancel common noise.
buy: More focused attention and less interference in the reported studies.
give: Two attention-map paths and additional training complexity; no guaranteed efficiency.
choose: Retrieval-heavy reasoning where distraction is a problem.
sourceTitle: Differential Transformer

name: Gated DeltaNet
problem: Delta writes still need a way to forget stale memory.
idea: Combine an adaptive decay gate with delta-rule memory corrections.
buy: Better retention/forgetting trade and small recurrent state.
give: A compressed state cannot provide exact random access to arbitrary old tokens.
choose: Streaming inference with adaptive state; often hybridized with attention.
sourceTitle: Gated Delta Networks: Improving Mamba2 with Delta Rule

name: Native Sparse Attention (NSA)
problem: Sparse methods can be hard to train efficiently on GPUs.
idea: Combine compressed global summaries, selected blocks and local windows in hardware-friendly kernels.
buy: Trainable long-context sparsity with local and global paths.
give: Dynamic selection and compression can omit relevant evidence.
choose: Long-context pretraining and deployment with specialized kernels.
sourceTitle: Native Sparse Attention: Hardware-Aligned and Natively Trainable Sparse Attention
note: NSA and later DSA are different designs; do not conflate them.

name: DeepSeek Sparse Attention (DSA)
problem: Long-context inference and training remain costly even with a small MLA KV cache.
idea: Use a lightweight indexer to select relevant cached token positions for fine-grained sparse attention.
buy: Computes much less query-to-key work than dense attention on long sequences.
give: Indexer adds complexity and can overlook weak-but-important evidence.
choose: Long-document and agent contexts with high recall requirements after validation.
sourceTitle: DeepSeek-V3.2-Exp: first public DeepSeek Sparse Attention release
formula: lightning indexer → selected top-k token positions
note: MLA (2024) compresses stored KV; DSA (2025) sparsifies which token positions are attended. Different optimization axes.

name: DroPE — drop positional embeddings
problem: RoPE can overfit to the training-length coordinate system.
idea: After pretraining, drop positional embeddings and briefly recalibrate instead of extending rotary frequencies.
buy: Proposed zero-shot context extension without long-window fine-tuning.
give: Needs recalibration, may sacrifice useful position cues; independent replication is important.
choose: Experimental retrofits for pretrained models; not a drop-in default.
sourceTitle: Extending the Context of Pretrained LLMs by Dropping Their Positional Embeddings
note: This is DroPE (dropping positional embeddings), not the unrelated DRoPE directional rotary embedding paper.
